dedupe_keys.name: ofcom uk home fixed line broadband performance measured speeds from a consumer panel

description: Ofcom's research on UK residential fixed-line broadband performance reports the actual speeds received by a panel of consumers who have speed monitoring units installed in their homes. The data show average download and upload speeds, latency and related measures for ADSL, cable and fibre packages, at national level and separately by package for the major internet service providers, and later reports add breakdowns by time of day, rurality and nation. The national data portal lists reports from May 2012 to November 2014 as PDF, a quarterly CSV update from February 2016 held in the National Archives web archive, and a link to Ofcom's broadband speeds index page with later editions; Ofcom publishes these data to give consumers and other stakeholders comparative information on performance. Coverage: the United Kingdom, from a sample of homes. Format and access: PDF reports and CSV data tables, free under the Open Government Licence. Caveats: a panel sample, not full coverage; later editions sit on Ofcom's site, which refused automated requests in this session, so their current format was not checked. Simulation uses: realistic speed and latency distributions by technology for service models, and baselines against which to detect degradation. Related records: Ofcom Connected Nations gives coverage, and Breitbandmessung and NetTest are crowdsourced measurement datasets in other countries.
name: Ofcom UK home (fixed-line) broadband performance: measured speeds from a consumer panel
